beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:hushed, wonder]A small island in the Gulf holds one of the densest ancient ^cemeteries on Earth: burial mounds, by the ^thousand.
[d:tension][act:the question, leaning in][tune:rise]Was it where a whole region sent its ^dead?

[d:calm][act:plain, orienting]This is ^Bahrain, the heart of the Bronze Age land of ^Dilmun. [act:steady, factual]Between about {2200|twenty-two hundred} and {1750|seventeen fifty} BCE, its people raised burial mounds by the ^thousand. [p:0.93][act:explaining, plain]Each one a low dome, four and a half to nine metres across, raised over a ^grave.

[d:build][go:2|0][p:0.93][act:quietly astonished]Nearly twelve thousand are protected ^today. [act:plain]There may once have been seventy-five ^thousand. [p:0.93][act:playful, doing the sum]Visit one of the survivors every minute@time, day and night, and you'd need more than eight ^days.

[d:build][act:presenting it, fair]Far more graves than one small island could fill, some scholars ^thought. [act:their reasoning, fair]Surely, they said, the dead were brought here from ^elsewhere. [act:storytelling]And old Sumerian texts called Dilmun a ^pure, holy land. [act:the leap, even][tune:rise]So, was it an island of the ^dead, for all of ^Arabia?

[d:build][act:building, precise]Then, from {1954|nineteen fifty-four}, Danish archaeologists started ^digging, season after season. [act:the reveal]They found what the theory ^lacked: towns, temples, and a ^harbour. [act:explaining, a simple picture]A cemetery tells you about the dead. [act:explaining, a simple picture]A town tells you who ^buried them. [act:the point, clear][tune:fall]The mounds were built by the island's own people, over five ^centuries.

[d:reveal][act:the reveal, delighted]And the biggest mounds, at ^A'ali, belonged to ^kings. [p:0.93][act:vivid]They're more than thirty metres across: wider than a tennis court is ^long. [act:precise]Stone vessels even give their ^names: Ri'mum, and Yagli-El, servant of the god ^Inzak. [act:warm, a small wonder]A king of Dilmun, named in his own ^words.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm][tune:rise]An island of the ^dead? [act:the verdict, firm][tune:fall]*Ruled ^out*. [act:fair, clear]The island had its own towns, and its own ^kings. [act:warm, the other half][tune:fall]An island of the ^living, who honoured their dead for five hundred ^years.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, gentle][tune:fall]And nearly four thousand years on, their kings still have their ^names.
